plan.reason: The PR adds a priority filter to the list endpoint. The repository `where` branch (repository.ts:9) and the router 422 branch (router.ts:15) are uncovered, and no test checks that a parsed priority reaches the repository or that an invalid one is rejected. Backend-only cases are planned; the remaining gaps are listed separately.

cases.behavior: list({priority}) restricts the Prisma query to that priority and keeps newest-first ordering; list() and list({}) add no where clause.
cases.requirementSource: openapi.json GET /api/todos 'priority' query parameter ('Filter tasks by priority.'); TodoStore.list(query?: TodoListQuery) in types.ts
cases.inputs: repository.list({ priority: 'low' }) with findMany mocked to return [record]; then repository.list({}) in the same test.
cases.expected: First findMany call receives { where: { priority: 'low' }, orderBy: [{ created_at: 'desc' }, { id: 'desc' }] }. Second call has no 'where' key. Result is mapped via fromModel.
cases.mockBoundary: vi.spyOn on the real Prisma delegate's findMany, as in the existing tests; no database.

existingTests.name: lists tasks in newest-first order and maps database rows

value.regression: The filter is dropped, so every task is returned. Or the filter is applied to the wrong column. Or the empty query adds where: { priority: undefined } instead of omitting it.
value.rationale: The existing test calls list() only, so the new where branch is untested. The filter is the PR's main behavior and needs one cheap spy-based case.

cases.behavior: GET /api/todos?priority=high parses the query and passes { priority: 'high' } to repository.list.
cases.requirementSource: openapi.json GET /api/todos 'priority' query parameter with enum low|medium|high
cases.expected: Status 200, body [todo], repository.list called once with { priority: 'high' }.
cases.mockBoundary: Fake TodoStore passed to createTodosRouter; supertest over an in-memory express app.

value.regression: The router ignores req.query and calls repository.list() with no filter, so clients always get every task.
value.rationale: The existing test only checks list was called once and cannot tell whether a priority was forwarded. The case reuses the existing setup.

cases.behavior: An out-of-enum priority query returns 422 with validation issues and never reaches the repository.
cases.requirementSource: openapi.json GET /api/todos response '422' (Invalid input) and the priority enum
cases.expected: Status 422; body.detail is a non-empty array; repository.list is not called.
cases.mockBoundary: Fake TodoStore and supertest, as in the existing router tests.

existingTests.name: rejects invalid patch body without updating: %j

value.regression: An invalid priority is silently ignored or passed through to the repository, giving a 200 or a Prisma error instead of the documented 422.
value.rationale: router.ts:15 is an uncovered branch and the documented 422 response is new in this PR. The test follows the existing invalid-input pattern at low cost.

cases.behavior: With no priority, and with unrelated query keys, the router passes an object with no priority key to repository.list.
cases.requirementSource: listQuerySchema in validators.ts makes priority optional; z.object strips unknown keys (characterization of the zod default, not a documented guarantee)
cases.assertion: expect(repository.list).toHaveBeenCalledWith({}) — a priority key with value undefined is not distinguishable by toHaveBeenCalledWith, so the case also checks Object.keys(repository.list.mock.calls[0][0]) is empty.

value.regression: Raw req.query is forwarded, so unrelated parameters leak to the repository. Or an unfiltered request becomes a filter with an invalid value.
value.rationale: The existing assertion, calledOnce, ignores the argument. Adding the argument check to the existing scenario costs one line.

remainingGaps: No test checks the openapi.json priority parameter or 422 response. factory.test.ts stubs the spec, so asserting document content there would need a real-file read and is not planned.
Repeated priority parameters (?priority=a&priority=b) produce an array under Express query parsing; the intended behavior is not specified, so no case is planned.
Frontend does not use the priority filter yet; no frontend cases are justified by this PR.
Pre-existing uncovered locations outside this PR (backend/src/main.ts, factory.ts:20, frontend AppProviders and others) were not analyzed.
